- Attached CSV (egress-ip-list.csv) enumerates the public egress IPs our Private control plane may use for control traffic and webhook callbacks when a private endpoint is configured. Each row includes IP, ASN, region, and "shared" flag.

Emily / team — technical addendum below (pasted from ops notes).

Summary:
- Primary egress set (control-plane) = 3 static /24 blocks and 6 ephemeral /32s depending on region; see CSV for exact addresses. Static blocks are announced by our partner ASN 34123; ephemeral addresses are NATed from transient pools.
- Dedicated (Reserved Egress) customers receive single-tenant elastic IPs that are dedicated to the account — those show as "dedicated" in the CSV.
- Shared-pool traffic is multi-tenant; we do NOT send customer data payloads to third-party endpoints except for optional telemetry. Control-plane messages include metadata-only heartbeats + encrypted TLS connections to your private endpoint.

Firewall recommendations (minimal):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to the CSV-listed IPs and CIDRs.
- Validate SNI on TLS for control-plane hostnames: ctrl.redwood-inference.net and alt-ctrl.redwood-inference.net.
- Allow DNS lookups to your resolver for any dynamic hostnames; for environments that block DNS, we can provide static A records.

Audit evidence we can provide:
- IP announcement proof: provider BGP snips + letter on provider letterhead (PDF).
- Historical connection logs for your test tenant (timeboxed) showing source IPs and timestamps (we can redact PII).
- Firewall rule diff from our baseline that shows the control-plane egress spike during a connector provisioning event (attached PDF).

Attachment: fw-rules-diff.pdf (stub)

Note: regarding "ownership" — some IPs are announced by our cloud peering partner; we will include documentation that maps the IP to the announcing AS and include who to contact at the provider. If FinHealth requires provider-signed ownership, we will coordinate and escalate.

— Irene
Irene Choi
